# Jev integration catalog (Claude Code relevance)

Generated 2026-09-30. 983 analysed entries (46 adversarially verified, 477 source-audited, 460 README-triaged), 519 listed in community awesome-lists but not analysed (off-target), 19 excluded.

Score: 0-10 for daily coding in Claude Code with OpenRouter-hosted Jev (verified or category-judge score when available). OR = OpenRouter support found in code. Tier: V = verified, S = source-audited, R = README-triaged.

## decision-mcp (124)

**Worth it:** situational. Placeholder
**Best pick:** FrancoisChastel/jev-code: Highest verified score (7). Native OpenRouter routing, small tool surface, no hooks to wedge a session, fail-visible errors, large test suite. Least-bad rather than trustworthy: it is 3 days old, has no npm provenance, is discretionary only, and needs TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL=jev-1.13 and a doctor --live check first.

## task-mcp (29)

**Worth it:** situational. The user's goal is Jev used automatically with no prompting. This category cannot meet that: every MCP or skill option is model-discretion, and the hook options are narrow or unusable as shipped. The project's own bench shows 0 of 150 auto-calls, and an agent-outcome study shows no accuracy gain and +4.6 s median. Jev quality is a poor fit for review and verification: Noul ECE is 0.169 and Choice 0.226 on 4,995 coding-agent decisions, and vulnerable-code accuracy is 71.5%. One appended line can flip accuracy from 96.5% to 26.5%. Diffs, logs and files go to OpenRouter and TypeSafe, and the alp…
**Best pick:** uditakhourii/quicksilver: Least-bad rather than trustworthy. It is the lowest-overhead verified option (no MCP, no hook, about 190 tokens always-on, config-only OpenRouter switch) and it targets Jev's real strength, bulk relevance triage. Use it only from a locally pinned, read-through copy with jev-1.13 pinned, a Bash allow rule for the exact qs.mjs path, and OPENROUTER_API_KEY plus the JEV_API_KEY alias added to the no-…

## permission-gate (60)

**Worth it:** situational. Anthropic's classifier plus the user's deny rules and no-secret-leak hook already gate most risk, and Jev is not a better judge (accuracy a bit below mid-price LLMs; 1.0 probability on 56% of answers, 9 of them wrong). Most 'auto-approver' repos remove prompts, which the user in auto and bypass modes mostly does not have, and PermissionRequest hooks and gates keyed on default/acceptEdits mode do nothing there. What remains is Jev as an add-only layer: deny or ask on things like out-of-scope commits, pushes, deploys or unrequested edits, especially in bypass sessions where a hook deny is the o…
**Best pick:** RiskAverseTech/toolgate: Least-bad verified option, not a strong endorsement. It is the only one that is automatic, natively OpenRouter (verified), can deny in bypass, and is actively maintained. Trial it in a narrowed setup: gated_tools set to Bash and Write only, unattended.ask set to ask, backend.provider pinned to openrouter, and OPENROUTER_API_KEY added to no-secret-leak first. Run it for 1 to 2 weeks on personal re…

## security-guard (36)

**Worth it:** situational. The idea fits the "automatic, no prompting" goal. Hooks are the one mechanism that fires without saying "use jev". But the evidence for this user is thin. (1) In bypassPermissions there are no prompts to save, and the audited plugins' tripwires only defer (verified for jev-bouncer), so only a Jev deny at p>=0.95 or an ask adds anything. The dr-dimitru plugin even suppresses ask in bypass mode. (2) In auto mode the Sonnet classifier is already a stronger judge and cannot be injected through tool results. A Jev allow would replace it for that call, weakening a layer. (3) Jev is documented as in…

## stop-verifier (29)

**Worth it:** situational. Upside: a Stop-time honesty check is the only place Jev integrates fully automatically. It is cheap, adds no per-tool-call latency (unlike your gitnexus hooks), works unattended in bypassPermissions sessions where a false "tests pass" claim costs most, and can be fail-open. Downsides: (1) Value is unproven. The only controlled A/B (jevwatch) showed no gain, Limpet's AUROC is 0.50-0.64, and independent evals show the high-probability band is reliable (p>=0.85 was right 100% in sec-bench) but calibration is poor, with 1.0 saturation and overconfidence on unanswerable inputs. That means false-po…
**Best pick:** greghavens/jev-no-bullshit: Highest verified score (7). It is a deterministic, fail-open, stdlib-only Stop hook that is OpenRouter-compatible with just TYPESAFE_BASE_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api plus the OpenRouter key in ~/.config/jev-no-bullshit/env (the hardcoded 'jev-latest' is accepted by OpenRouter). It has real tests and CI, and needs no prompting. It is least-bad rather than trustworthy: no LICENSE, unredacted defa…

## review-ci (57)

**Worth it:** situational. The category is worth a bounded trial in personal repos, not a global install. Pro: hook-driven tools genuinely satisfy "automatic", fire under bypassPermissions (PreToolUse denies and PostToolUse still run), and cost about $0.0001 per check with 200-600 ms latency. Con: (1) Jev is measurably weaker than Opus or Sonnet at code judgment and is overconfident, so it produces both false alarms and misses, and injection in the code being judged can suppress findings. (2) Every checked edit or commit sends full source to OpenRouter and then TypeSafe, which is a consent and NDA problem for client pr…
**Best pick:** JevGate (Tech-Byte-Frontier/jevgate): Least-bad rather than trustworthy. It is the only tool that is both fully automatic (hooks fire with no prompting, fail open, verified against v0.32.0 source) and natively OpenRouter-capable. But it is 12 days old, has a single maintainer and a force-pushed main, had 50-63% 503s on OpenRouter, writes Git objects into every repo, and has a bare-'jevgate' PATH problem. Use it only project-scoped in…

## code-search-nav (33)

**Worth it:** situational. The value is real but narrow. Jev is cheap (about $0.042 per 1M input tokens) and fast (p50 about 200 ms), and semantic screening of many files or hunks is something Grep cannot do. Against that: Opus plus gitnexus already answers most 'where is X' questions better, and Jev's independent evals show accuracy below mid-price LLMs, overconfidence (exactly 1.0 on 56% of answers) and vulnerability to injected file text. The larger blocker is privacy. Every tool uploads source chunks to OpenRouter and TypeSafe on the /alpha endpoint (no SLA), most with only filename-based secret filtering, and in y…
**Best pick:** oko (bartlomein): Least-bad and the only near-automatic option: alwaysLoad MCP tool plus non-blocking hooks, verified to work on OpenRouter by setting TYPESAFE_BASE_URL alone. Still 12-day-old single-author alpha code that uploads snippets and installs per project, so pin a release, try it on a personal repo first, and never on client repos.

## dev-skill (61)

**Worth it:** situational. The category does not deliver what you want, which is automatic Jev use. All 62 members are either knowledge skills or model-discretion CLI wrappers, and Opus rarely reaches for Jev in ordinary coding. The hook-shaped items are templates, not integrations. A PermissionRequest hook is the official cookbook pattern, but it fires only when a permission prompt would show. That means never in bypassPermissions, and in auto mode only for ask rules or hook-forced asks. A PreToolUse gate can only deny or ask in practice, so it adds latency and prompts and removes none. Jev quality also caps the upsid…
**Best pick:** okooo5km/jev: Least-bad option, not a real answer to your goal. It is the most auditable OpenRouter-native, zero-dependency, well-tested client (verified). Vendor the single file, pin JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter in the settings env block, and use it as a building block for your own hook, with --timeout 3 --retries 0. It does not make Claude use Jev automatically.

## prompt-steering (23)

**Worth it:** situational. Nothing here covers general daily coding. The value is narrow: enforcing prose rules from CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md that linters cannot check (for example "don't commit unless asked"), or a shadow-mode permission helper. The independent evidence supports Jev only for bounded, text-recoverable decisions. Action gate was 100/111 vs 102/111 for Opus. Tool-call risk was 55/60. The p>=0.85 band was right in sec-bench. It fails on ambiguous or unanswerable input, out-of-distribution shift (a dependency auto-merge gate had 15 unsafe merges), and injected approval text. Every gating design must therefore b…
**Best pick:** coldteadotai/abide: Highest verified score (7). It is automatic, fail-open, bounded, near-zero context cost, project-scopable, and reaches OpenRouter with env vars only (bare jev-latest is mapped by OpenRouter docs). Use it only on personal repos, and only after fixing these gaps. First, install it globally at a stable path with an absolute node path. Second, keep the base URL only in ~/.abide/.env, never a repo .en…

## context-pruning (37)

**Worth it:** situational. The payoff is small and the risks are real for this user. Safe operating points hide little. Winnow's author data shows 2-5% of text hidden at the safe threshold. jev-lens gets 79% overall but only 31% on code, and its 88% on command output is mostly the kind that rule-based head/tail filters already handle. Opus 5.5 does Read-then-Edit work, where a lossy view is the costly failure. Jev is overconfident (exactly 1.0 on 56% of answers, 9 of them wrong) and injectable, so a hostile log or file can hide lines from Opus. The larger cost is data egress. Every large Bash, Read, grep or MCP result …
**Best pick:** compactio (RamaAditya49): Least-bad option, not a trustworthy default. It is the only verified candidate that is a plain command-hook PostToolUse integration using OPENROUTER_API_KEY natively, fully automatic and fail-open. It has tight timeouts (1.5s Jev, 5s hook), never cuts Read of code files, and redacts what it sends to Jev. Use it hooks-only on personal projects: replace bare `node` with an absolute path, add OPENRO…

## compaction-memory (42)

**Worth it:** situational. The narrow upside is faster, verbatim compaction and per-prompt memory recall. The downsides for this user are heavy. (1) Every real compaction integration depends on the undocumented function-hooks flag, and nothing has been verified on 2.1.285. It may break silently on update. (2) They send tool inputs (bash commands, diffs, Write content, file paths) and prompts to a no-SLA /alpha OpenRouter endpoint and then TypeSafe, with only regex secret masking. That is a real client-confidentiality issue under auto and bypassPermissions sessions, where many unreviewed commands run. Only ingebyd pins …
**Best pick:** jevmem (avinash-jetwani): Least-bad and best fit, not trustworthy enough for client work. It is the highest verified score (6.5) and the only automatic integration on stable documented command hooks, with no function-hooks flag. It is opt-in per project, fail-open, and has a documented OpenRouter base-URL swap. Use it only on personal, trusted repos with a pinned version. Do not enable it in client repos because of the pe…

## model-router (103)

**Worth it:** situational. For this user the category is mostly not worth it, and it is not what the user asked for. Opus 5.5 is already the top tier and the login is a flat-rate subscription. So routing can only downgrade quality (Sonnet or Haiku on a real task) or lower effort, and cost savings barely matter. Jev's independent evals show accuracy a bit below mid-price LLMs, overconfidence on short or ambiguous prompts, and steerability by injected text. Those are exactly the weaknesses a prompt classifier meets. The proxy tools (switchboard, dirien, automodel, jevcc) put a single-maintainer, days-old binary in front …
**Best pick:** davila7 claude-code-templates: jev-model-router mod (subagent routing only): This is the least-bad option, not a strong one. It is the only automatic Jev router that needs no ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL proxy, keeps OAuth traffic direct to Anthropic, and is verified fail-open on the router half. Use it with routeMainEffort off, run it in observe mode first, put the key in via /config, copy only the jev-model-router mod folder, and skip the sibling skill-suggestion mod. It rests on…

## skill-tool-router (52)

**Worth it:** no. Benefit is marginal and unproven for this setup. Opus 5.5 already selects skills from native descriptions, and the user has only ~13 personal skills. Plugin skills (caveman, anthropic-skills) are often not even scanned by these tools. Every hook adds 0.3-2 s of synchronous latency to every prompt, stacked on the caveman UserPromptSubmit hook and the gitnexus hooks. Every prompt (and often recent transcript and skill descriptions) leaves the machine, which is a real confidentiality problem for client projects. The existing no-secret-leak guard does not cover UserPromptSubmit and does not list …
**Best pick:** jev-pilot (Akramovic1): Least-bad, not trustworthy enough for a global default. It is the only verified candidate that is automatic and native to OpenRouter (/api/v1/systemone), and it fails open with a 1.5 s race timeout. Use it only as a cautious trial. Install by hand and pin the reviewed commit e61f801. Skip curl/bash and the claude-jev proxy. Set hideListing=false, designPack=false and routeMainEffort=false. Set CL…

## suite-plugin (56)

**Worth it:** situational. As installable suites, mostly no. As a building block for a small self-written hook, situational. Against installing one: - Evidence is thin. The only end-to-end benchmark (Gilbert09, 1,176 sessions) is haiku/sonnet only, shows no gain on Sonnet and never tested Opus. klukacin logged about 18,000 decisions, found 126 minutes of added Bash-gate latency and no prevented incidents, then abandoned the plugin. griffinwork40/claude-jev measured 9.3% false blocks on real accepted edits. - The user's habits neutralise most of the value. In bypassPermissions there is no prompt for a gate to save. A ho…
**Best pick:** garygentry/system1: Least-bad, not trustworthy enough for unattended use. It is the only suite that is both verified OpenRouter-native and fail-open with near-zero context cost. Use it only with SYSTEM1_ENDPOINT pinned in the environment, a dedicated low-limit OpenRouter key, and .system1/config.yaml reviewed in every freshly cloned repo, or kept off client repos. Without the pin, a cloned repo can redirect your Ope…

## library-harness (63)

**Worth it:** situational. Nothing here delivers "automatic when it adds value" out of the box. Most members are SDKs for other stacks, and the Claude Code ones are per-project, alpha, days old, and self-benchmarked. In your auto mode the native classifier already decides most Bash calls, and PermissionRequest hooks only see the residual ask-path, so the friction Jev could remove is small. In bypass sessions there are no prompts to remove, so the only useful role is a deny/ask PreToolUse tripwire, which deterministic regex already does better. Jev's limits matter: 89.7-96.5% injection detection with context, accuracy 7…
**Best pick:** @typesafe-ai/sdk (official TypeScript SDK), as the base of a self-written hook: Least-bad, not trustworthy as a packaged integration. It is the only verified item that is vendor-blessed for OpenRouter (baseURL https://openrouter.ai/api, model jev-1.13 pinned), dependency-free, telemetry-free and gives typed errors for clean fail-open. Nothing in the category is safe or calibrated enough to install as an off-the-shelf gate. A plain fetch hook following the OpenRouter cookbook…
